summary:
We developed an intelligent, autonomous health and life-support monitoring app for astronauts during spacewalks (EVAs) and space exploration missions.

Currently, an astronaut's medical data and the spacesuit's life-support sensors are separated into isolated systems, leaving astronauts reliant on doctors on Earth to interpret their health. Our app solves this problem by combining both data streams into one simple, real-time platform. Working locally without needing a constant connection to Earth, it analyzes body and suit data together to give astronauts clear, early warnings on a simple screen, alongside a full dashboard for Mission Control.

This project is important because future missions to the Moon and Mars will have long communication delays with Earth, making real-time medical support from the ground impossible. By giving astronauts instant, easy-to-understand health alerts directly inside their suit, our app keeps them safer and more independent in deep space.
details:
Akari-1 is an autonomous causility motor that unifies an astronaut's biomedical telemetry with the spacesuit's life support sensors in real time. Also creating a harness that measure the glucose.

How does it work?

The app collects data provided by the sensors, analyzes it in real time, and displays it on the screen. These sensors monitor key indicators such as blood pressure, body temperature, ionizing radiation, oxygen saturation (SpO2), and blood glucose. Additionally, if a health abnormality is detected, the device triggers an alert indicating which parameter is out of range and communicates the specific type of medical issue. 

Benefits:

Elimination of health data latency: Astronauts can view their health status in real time without needing to communicate with Mission Control.

24/7 continuous monitoring: Crew members can wear the biometric harness at all times to detect early signs of and prevent silent health conditions.

Preliminary assessment and diagnosis: The application provides preliminary insights into conditions that pose a risk to the astronaut's health and offers preventive recommendations to avoid complications.

Automated emergency alarm: If the user experiences a medical issue that prevents them from treating themselves, the system immediately alerts fellow crew members to provide assistance.

Inteended Impact:

The intended impact of your app is to transform the spacesuit from a reactive life-support machine into a proactive, self-reliant health ecosystem, significantly increasing astronaut safety and operational autonomy during spacewalks (EVAs) and deep-space exploration.

Development tools:

Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Hosting: Deployed on Vercel using GoDaddy domains provided through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, with GitHub for version control and code management.
3D Modeling & Design: Hardware components modeled in SolidWorks, with realistic rendering and visualization using Blender.

Creativity and Innovation:

This project innovates through a dual-interface architecture that adapts a single technological platform to two completely different operational realities. On one hand, it provides the astronaut with a clean, high-contrast display on their forearm or visor, enabling glanceable health checks without navigating complex menus during critical tasks. On the other hand, it equips Mission Control with a comprehensive analytical dashboard featuring trend charts and color-coded alerts to monitor long-term risks, such as cardiovascular strain. All processing runs autonomously inside the suit itself, overcoming communication delays of up to 24 minutes in deep-space or Mars missions and transforming the suit into a true preventive medical assistant. 

Considerations:

- Intituive Design: Designed to be visually appealing and easy for anyone to use

-Daily Use: Planned to be trully comfortable for every day use

In summary Akari-1 is more than just an app is a step foward for the health maintenance in aerospace fields, always looking to prioritize good health above anything else.
